topic_tag: a ministry's response to a river flood
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In a later account, one reporter described the national ministry's response to the flood as ______.

worlds.passage: In the spring of 1974 a river broke through its levees and flooded some four hundred homes in a farming district. Within a week the ministry had set aside enough money to rebuild every damaged home. To receive any of it, a family had to file a separate claim for each room, attach an estimate from a licensed surveyor, and wait for a regional office to approve the claim, which came back unread if one box was blank; most families were paid the following spring. In a later account, one reporter described the national ministry's response to the flood as ______.
worlds.explanation: The money was ready within a week, and what held it back for a year was a chain of forms, estimates, and office approvals, so the response was "bureaucratic." "Crude" fails because claims were assessed room by room, the opposite of a rough one-size measure; "covert" fails because the aid ran through a public claims office with nothing hidden; "complacent" fails because the ministry moved quickly to fund every home rather than resting on past success.

crude.quote: a separate claim for each room
crude.why: Payments were measured to each room's damage, which is careful, not rough or unrefined.

covert.quote: wait for a regional office to approve
covert.why: Families dealt openly with the ministry's own offices; nothing about the aid was concealed.

complacent.quote: Within a week the ministry had set aside
complacent.why: The ministry acted promptly and funded full rebuilding; it did not treat the flood as needing no action.

worlds.passage: In the spring of 1974 a river broke through its levees and flooded some four hundred homes in a farming district. The ministry's engineers noted that the same levees had held through three higher floods in the previous forty years. On that record the ministry judged the break a freak event, turned down the district's request to raise the levees, and paid only to close the gap where the water had come through and nothing more. In a later account, one reporter described the national ministry's response to the flood as ______.
worlds.explanation: Reassured by the levees' past record, the ministry treated the break as a fluke and saw no need to do more, so its response was "complacent." "Crude" fails because the ministry did very little, not something rough; the one repair is not described as clumsy; "covert" fails because its judgment and its refusal were stated to the district openly; "bureaucratic" fails because no forms, claims, or approvals stood between anyone and aid: the request was simply refused.

crude.quote: paid only to close the gap
crude.why: The fault is how little was done, not that what was done was rough or unrefined.

covert.why: The ministry answered the district directly; its decision was not hidden.

bureaucratic.quote: On that record the ministry judged
bureaucratic.why: The response turned on a judgment drawn from the levees' record, not on procedures or paperwork.

worlds.passage: In the spring of 1974 a river broke through its levees and flooded some four hundred homes in a farming district. Engineers at the ministry knew that a drainage canal it had dug the year before had weakened the levee at the very point where it broke. Rather than admit this, the ministry paid each family through a church charity that did not name its source, and reporters learned where the money had come from only twelve years later. In a later account, one reporter described the national ministry's response to the flood as ______.
worlds.explanation: Because its own canal had caused the break, the ministry hid its role by sending the money through a charity that never named it, so the response was "covert." "Crude" fails because nothing is said of the aid being rough or poorly judged, only of its source being hidden; "complacent" fails because the ministry knew it was at fault and acted; "bureaucratic" fails because the money reached families directly through the charity without forms or approvals.

crude.quote: paid each family through a church charity
crude.why: The point of the arrangement is concealment of the source, not a rough or unrefined method of aid.

complacent.why: The ministry knew its own canal caused the break and paid for it; it was not resting easy on a good record.

bureaucratic.why: The ministry routed aid quietly through a charity, which is the opposite of an official procedure families had to work through.

worlds.passage: In the spring of 1974 a river broke through its levees and flooded some four hundred homes in a farming district. The ministry acted within a day, sending trucks of sandbags and a check for one fixed sum to every household. A family whose cellar had taken a foot of water received what a family whose house had washed away received, and the sandbags were tipped out at the roadside, unfilled and unstacked, for each household to place itself. In a later account, one reporter described the national ministry's response to the flood as ______.
worlds.explanation: The ministry acted fast and openly, with one flat payment regardless of loss and sandbags simply dumped, so the response was "crude": rough and unrefined. "Covert" fails because the trucks and checks came openly from the ministry; "complacent" fails because it acted within a day; "bureaucratic" fails because every household was paid at once with no claims or approvals.

covert.why: The aid arrived openly from the ministry itself, with nothing hidden about its source.

complacent.why: An immediate response rules out a ministry satisfied that nothing needed doing.

bureaucratic.quote: one fixed sum to every household
bureaucratic.why: Every household received the same check without filing or assessment, so no procedure slowed the aid.
